deities: 13-ft monolithic idol embodying the Trimurti: Brahma at the base, Shiva in the middle, Vishnu at the top

history.dynasty: None - modern shrine (Zamindari era; Kirlampudi estate)
history.summary: A Vaishnavite temple on 300-ft Ratnagiri Hill beside the Pampa river. Origin legend: Vishnu appeared in simultaneous dreams of devotee Eeranki Prakasa Rao and Raja Inuganti Venkata Rama Rayanam Bahadur (zamindar of Gorasa, Kirlampudi estate), and the idol was found under an Ankudu (Krishna Kutaja) tree and consecrated 6 Aug 1891 (Khara year, Sravana Sukla Vidiya) with the Sri Matripada Vibhuti Maha Vaikuntha Narayana Yantra brought from Kashi. The temple is built in the form of a chariot with four wheels at the corners and four pillars symbolising the four Vedas. Considered Andhra Pradesh's second-most-visited temple after Tirupati. Sub-shrines on the hill include Sri Rama, Vana Durga and Kanaka Durga.

name: Sri Veera Venkata Satyanarayana Swamy Temple
town_description: Annavaram is a pilgrimage town in Kakinada district of coastal Andhra Pradesh, at the foot of the 300-ft Ratnagiri Hill on the banks of the Pampa river. The town's economy revolves around the Satyanarayana Swamy Devasthanam; the hill-top temple, Pampa Sarovara boating point and the ghat road/steps make it a major religious hub. It is about 45 km from Kakinada, 30 km from Pithapuram and 108 km from Visakhapatnam.

travel.airport: Visakhapatnam International Airport (~108 km); Rajahmundry Airport is closer (~85 km, verify).
travel.railway: Annavaram railway station on the Chennai-Kolkata (Howrah-Chennai) main line, about 4-5 km from the temple; autos/buses to the hill base.
travel.road: On the Chennai-Kolkata highway (NH-16); a ghat road plus about 300 stone steps lead to the Ratnagiri summit.

visitor_information.best_time: October to March (cooler weather); heavy rush during Karthika Masam and Kalyanotsavam (April-May).
visitor_information.opening_hours: Sources conflict - verify on the official portal: travel guides cite 6:00 AM-12:30 PM and 1:00-9:00 PM (Sarva Darshan); one devotional channel cites 3:30 AM-9:00 PM. Satyanarayana Vratam generally 6:00 AM-6:00 PM.
